**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  [Javaagent] Log failures suppressed while wrapping**

If proxy generation fails unexpectedly, `suppress = Throwable.class` silently discards the wrapping failure, leaving no diagnostic for why the context-propagation protection did not take effect. Catch and log the failure where wrapping occurs while preserving the original executor, as required for fallible advice helpers. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  [Javaagent] Drop the return-type matcher**

The HikariPool type has a single zero-argument `initializeHouseKeepingExecutorService` lifecycle method, so this `returns(...)` clause neither selects a supported overload nor prevents a concrete incompatibility; the typed `@Advice.Return` and replacement do not justify it. Match by name or zero-argument signature and remove the static import. Does it work / is it any better to use `ignoreTaskClass(...)` like OkHttp, or make `Context.root()` current around maintenance-task submission like MongoDB, instead of proxying the executor?

replies.body: I think `ignoreTaskClass` worked but had to use `HikariPool$Lambda` which didn't feel ideal as it is hard to tell whether there are any other lambdas in that class that could benefit from propagation. Handling submission wasn't easy as `createPoolEntry` first calls `newPoolEntry`, for which context could be propagated to get statements executed to initialize connection added to the calling trace, and later submits a task to the housekeeping executor, for which propagation isn't wanted. I guess we could set root context around the method and accept that whatever is executed to initialize the connection will be in a separate trace.
